subject: Dedicated reservation options — GPU baseline, staggered onramp & procurement milestones
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@orionbio.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation options — GPU baseline, staggered onramp & procurement milestones

Claire —

Thanks again for the time this week. Per our call I sketched three practical reservation options that balance OrionBio's bursty inference profile and procurement timing. I attached a spreadsheet with the line-by-line economics, and pulled key points below so your ops/procurement teams can review quickly.

Top-line options (summary):
- Option A — Conservative baseline: 24 GPUs dedicated (min floor), burst to 48 via queued burst windows. Lower monthly commit, slower warm-up cadence. Good if you want strict cost caps and can tolerate queueing during peak bursts.
- Option B — Performance-first stagger: Start at 48 GPUs with scheduled ramps to 96 across three months. Includes 10% warm-start credit and 3 canary prewarm windows. Better latency SLOs during initial launch.
- Option C — Elastic anchor: 32 GPUs guaranteed, 64 on-call reserved buffer, with automated geo-failover. Designed for predictable latency with moderate cost.

Key procurement milestones I recommend including in contract:
1) Activation window (30 days from signature)
2) Month 1 canary and SLA check-in
3) Warm-start credits applied within first billing cycle
4) Optional step-up clause for month 3 and month 6

Please review the attached "OrionBio_Dedicated_Options_Q327.xlsx" — sheet 1 has the scenario matrix and token-cost burn forecasts using OrionBio's sample traffic. If this looks directionally right, we can convert Option B into a proposal doc and route to your procurement for comments.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the spreadsheet.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Claire Huang <claire@orionbio.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops_lead@orionbio.com, procurement@orionbio.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options — GPU baseline, staggered onramp & procurement milestones

Karthik —

Thanks, this is very helpful. A few quick notes from ops and procurement after a skim:
- Ops: They like Option B latency guarantees but want a clearer ramp schedule (exact dates for the 48 -> 72 -> 96 steps) and an explanation of how KV cache warmup will be handled across nodes during the ramp.
- Procurement: Wants the activation window reduced to 21 days and would prefer a 60-day cancellation notice for the first 3 months instead of month-to-month. Also asked whether warm-start credits can be pro-rated if we activate mid-billing cycle.

Can you put together a short timeline we can attach to the SOW (dates + criteria for each ramp step)? Also share the SLA table you mentioned (even a one-page PDF is fine).

Best,
Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Platform Operations, OrionBio
claire@orionbio.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated reservation options — GPU baseline, staggered onramp & procurement milestones

Marissa / Monica —

Forwarding OrionBio's initial feedback. They like Option B but want explicit ramp dates, KV warmup behavior, and procurement tweaks (21-day activation window, 60-day cancellation notice for first 3 months, pro-rated credits).

Questions for you:
1) Can we commit to a strict 21-day activation target for Option B with our current cluster provisioning lead times? Any risk to the SLA if we shorten the activation window?
2) For KV cache warmup: recommend we state the warm-start plan as incremental node-level warming with targeted prefix caching for the first two weeks. Monica — can you add an ops-approved paragraph that explains the warmup plan and expected cold-latency curve (P50/P95) during week 1 and week 2?
3) On cancellation notice: legal usually accepts 60-day notice with pro-rated credits — can we offer a pro-rate clause for warm-start credits if activation occurs mid-billing cycle?

I'll assemble a simple timeline and an SLA one-pager once I have answers.

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated reservation options — GPU baseline, staggered onramp & procurement milestones

Karthik / Marissa —

Quick ops notes for the timeline/SLA:
- Activation timing: 21 days is feasible if we receive signed SOW + capacity reservation request by EOD week 0 and confirm cluster flavor (A100s 80GB vs H100s) within 48 hrs. Risk: supply-side delays if our procurement queue is saturated; we should call out an activation SLA exception for hardware allocation delays (we'll include an "activation-at-risk" flag in the SOW).
- Ramp schedule (Option B concrete proposal):
  * Day 0 (activation): 48 GPUs live (canary subset of traffic at 10%)
  * Day 14: increase to 64 GPUs; apply first warm-start credit; expand traffic to 35%
  * Day 30: increase to 80 GPUs; full production split; second warm-start credit applied
  * Day 90: step to 96 GPUs if agreed step-up clause exercised
- KV warmup plan: prefix-level cache seeding plus hot-key pinning for first 72 hours; targeted KV replication across nodes on Day 7 to avoid cold-cache storms. Expect P50 inference latency to start near the hosted baseline + ~6–8ms on Day 0, P95 may be up to +130ms then fall to within +40ms by Day 14 and align with baseline by Day 30.
- Pro-rated credits: we can pro-rate warm-start credits when activation occurs mid-cycle; legal to confirm final language.

I'll draft a short paragraph for the SOW and a one-page SLA figure.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Solutions Ops, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options — GPU baseline, staggered onramp & procurement milestones

Claire —

Per your asks, attached are: (1) a one-page SLA PDF that lists activation targets, latency expectations during warmup, and the exception clause for activation delays; (2) an updated option B timeline embedded in the XLSX with exact dates and gating criteria. Summary below so procurement can paste into the SOW:

Proposed SOW excerpt (Option B):
- Activation: signed SOW + reservation confirmation triggers a 21-calendar-day activation window. If hardware allocation delay occurs, Redwood will notify OrionBio within 72 hours and the parties will agree to an activation-at-risk date.
- Ramp steps and gating: Day 0 = 48 GPUs (10% canary); Day 14 = 64 GPUs (35% traffic) contingent on canary error/latency gates; Day 30 = 80 GPUs (full split) contingent on SLA checks; Day 90 = optional step-up to 96 GPUs per written request and billing amendment.
- Warm-start credits: 10% of month 1 committed spend applied pro-rated if activation is mid-cycle.
- Cancellation: 60-day notice required for first 90 days; standard 30-day thereafter.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement to confirm activation window/cancellation language.
2) Ops to sign off on the KV warmup paragraph (Monica already drafted).
3) If procurement agrees, I'll convert Option B into a formal proposal and generate the DocuSign packet (link included).

Thanks — looking forward to finishing SOW language so we can lock an activation date.

Best,
Karthik
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
